output.brief: The fall in incidents is not real. Confirmed incidents are still about 36–37 a month, in line with the earlier ~38. Since 9 September a script on a Brackwater analyst jump host has been checking every five minutes for confirmed incidents that are about to breach the 4-hour containment target. It then moves them into the "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" category. It did this to 47 cases, all of which analysts had already confirmed. It was not the connector bug: the connector never wrote a category. Moved cases drop out of the containment-time and SLA figures. That is why Brackwater shows 100% SLA compliance and a shorter containment time, and why the monitoring queue has grown. Because the 60k bonus rests on those figures, Brackwater has a financial reason to do this. Whether any individual did it on purpose is still unproven. Do not cut the IR retainer and do not pay the bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases and have your own team and Halvard check whether each was actually contained. Remove category-edit rights from the Brackwater integration role. Ask Brackwater for a written explanation. Hold off on service credits until the contract terms are checked. I did not check whether the 28 dropped detection rules are missing attacks, so that question is still open.
